title: Higgs Diary
summary: A 23-week self-study journey from linear algebra to the Higgs boson. The diary itself is private; this page shows live progress.
body:
Starting point: Calculus I and Physics I done, linear algebra half-way. Goal: understand the Higgs mechanism conceptually and rebuild the **H → ZZ → 4ℓ** discovery plot from real data.

| Phase | Weeks | Focus |
|---|---|---|
| 1 · Math foundations | 1–8 | Linear algebra, complex vectors, multivariable calculus, ODEs, probability |
| 2 · Physics bridge | 9–13 | Waves, EM, special relativity, four-vectors, fitting |
| 3 · Quantum + nuclear | 14–17 | Schrödinger equation, operators, spin, detectors |
| 4 · Particle physics | 18–20 | Standard Model, Feynman diagrams, cross sections, Z peak |
| 5 · Higgs | 21–23 | Symmetry breaking, 125 GeV peak, 5σ |

The daily notes live in a password-protected, encrypted diary that only I can open.

title: Finding the Z boson peak
summary: Invariant mass of muon pairs from CERN open data, with a fit of the Z resonance at ~91 GeV.
body:
Planned for week 20 of the Higgs Diary. Build a function that computes the invariant mass

$$M^2 = (E_1+E_2)^2 - |\vec p_1 + \vec p_2|^2$$

for every muon pair, histogram it, and fit the peak.

title: Rediscovering the Higgs in H → ZZ → 4ℓ
summary: Select four-lepton events, compare data to signal + background simulation and compute the significance of the 125 GeV bump.
body: The final project of the program (weeks 21–23): a one-page report with goal, method, plot and result.
